Common questions

Frequently asked questions

I already have a financial advisor. Why do I need this?+
Most clients do. The difference is coordination: we stress-test your income, audit fees and taxes, and tie investments, insurance, and estate together — the questions a "money manager" rarely answers.
Is this a sales pitch for products?+
No. We're fiduciaries. The assessment and review are educational; any recommendation is based on what's right for your plan, never a commission.
What is the Retirement Red Zone Stress Test?+
It shows how your accounts and withdrawal plan would hold up if a major market drop hit early in retirement — so you understand your real risk before it matters.
How much do I need to get started?+
We typically work with households with $2M–$10M in investable assets, though the right fit always depends on your specific situation and goals.
What does being a fiduciary mean?+
We're legally and ethically required to act in your best interest — coordinating your full plan rather than selling products.
How quickly will someone follow up?+
If you qualify, a fiduciary specialist typically reaches out within one business day to schedule your strategy session.
